canonical_record.label: Fluent counterfactuals for attribution-faithfulness evaluation
canonical_record.summary: Kamahi et al. (2024) argue that removing or corrupting input tokens creates out-of-distribution inputs for autoregressive language models and propose fluent in-distribution counterfactuals for evaluating attribution methods.

sources.title: Counterfactuals As a Means for Evaluating Faithfulness of Attribution Methods in Autoregressive Language Models

statement: Kamahi et al. (2024) argue that removing or corrupting input tokens creates out-of-distribution inputs for autoregressive language models and propose fluent in-distribution counterfactuals for evaluating attribution methods.

scope.population: Autoregressive language models in the authors’ proposed evaluation
scope.assumptions: Authors’ methodological argument, without quantitative validation in the retained abstract

support.quote: Most faithfulness evaluation techniques corrupt or remove input tokens deemed important by a particular attribution (feature importance) method and observe the resulting change in the model’s output.
However, for autoregressive language models, this approach creates out-of-distribution inputs due to their next-token prediction training objective.
Our technique generates fluent, in-distribution counterfactuals, making the evaluation protocol more reliable.

support.quote: This issue is particularly severe in cases of knowledge conflict, where the retrieved context conflicts with the model’s parametric knowledge.
